pointOfInterests.description: This put in is open as of December 2025, following a 16 month closure by the US Forest Service. It is a vast expanse of packed gravel left behind by CSX after Hurricane Helene. Enjoy the site responsibly. It will be redeveloped into a more formal put in in the future.
pointOfInterests.name: Poplar Put In

pointOfInterests.description:
Shortly after passing underneath the railroad trestle the river takes a decided hard left denoting the beginning of Entrance. Enter center or just right of center & then pick your way down depending on the water level be aware of two holes towards the bottom left. From 2000 c.f.s on up this rapid gets to be a pushy sucker. If you flip here, tuck tight & roll quick as this rapid has you moving fast and can be a bit shallow in places. Excellent recovery pool at the bottom.

Alternate Lines - At flows starting around 2000 c.f.s. a nice little creeky boof move opens up on the far left - not a good place to practice boofing as there a couple large flat rocks not far away. Even farther left, not far off the bank is another creeky little line with a couple small eddies.

Play factor - some. At higher flows a couple really fast, wide waves at the bottom are a ton of fun if you can catch them. At really low levels, the lowest hole on the left, known as Punk Hole, becomes a good little cartwheel spot.
pointOfInterests.name: Last Chance a.k.a. Entrance

pointOfInterests.description: Post-Helene: On the Rocks now features a fun fairly straight line down the main river left channel. In the first stage of the rapid, there is an obvious horizon line: go left to avoid a hole or boof straight off the middle for a bit of air time and a hole-punch. The second stage of the rapid has an undercut rock on river right that has pinned rafts, so keep some left momentum in the second part of this rapid.
pointOfInterests.name: On The Rocks

pointOfInterests.description: As described by William Nealy, "a single sloping ledge terminated by a huge cresent shaped hole." That pretty much nails it, even post-Helene. Jaws is a GREAT place to spend the afternoon surfing. Tuck tight when you flip upstream because the rock shelf causing the hole is never very far away no matter the level...it's been known to munch more than a few paddles. Good eddy access from the right. At higher flows Jaws could be called III+ due to its violent sticky nature but plenty of people still like to get a chunky slice of it. Hurricane Helene moved a new rock a few boat lengths downstream of Jaws on its left side, which has made the hole stickier and more symetrical, with less of a sneak and easy out on the left.
pointOfInterests.name: Jaws

pointOfInterests.description: Hurricane Helene totally remade Quarter-mile into a shorter steeper rapid. Approaching the rapid a horizon line is very obvious. Eddy out to scout or portage on the left. The top drop is a powerful 3-5 foot vertical ledge that can be run far left or center. At medium and higher flows a sneak opens up on the far right of the river that bypasses the ledge. The second drop can either be run down a relatively easy far left slide or it can be run right of the boulder for a juicy left to right curler ride.
pointOfInterests.name: Quarter Mile

pointOfInterests.description: Roostertail is wildly fun and totally different than the pre-helene version. It starts off with an excellent low angle surf hole. The first ledge can be run several ways, including down the left, just left of the big hole. The middle ledge can also be run left of the center rock or right of it. The final ledge offers a fun water boof into the right eddy, which is where the old main drop of roostertail used to be. It still dishes out enders.
pointOfInterests.name: Roostertail

pointOfInterests.description: There are a few rapids in the area now, but most importantly CSX created a new rapid when they filled in most of the river with rocks, forcing all of the water into a 5 foot drop with a nasty hole and undercut. Scout right. Paddlers are running down the left tongue with some left angle at low flows, sometimes starting from river right and cutting behind the boulder just upstream of the drop, and are running right of the undercut at medium and high flows.
pointOfInterests.name: Rollercoaster (NEW)

pointOfInterests.description: This ledge is more in the II+/III- range depending on your route; several of which can be taken. The straightforward route is following the main flow through some bouncy water on the river left. Route #2 is to work over to far, far river right and go through a narrow 3 ft chute. Route #3 which is the least easy to identify is to take a mini slide from right to left just to the right of an exposed rock formation found left of center.
pointOfInterests.name: Surprise

pointOfInterests.description: After Surprise the river bed slowly starts getting more congested requiring one to scent out the path of least resistance. This congestion continues to build till the main flow is on river left, after about 300 yards of this, the river bends right into a mega pile of boulders requiring careful navigation to avoid busting up your boat at lower levels and to avoid an ugly broach at any level. Keep it straight throught here. Helene changed this rapid, but not enough...
pointOfInterests.name: Rock Garden

pointOfInterests.description: This rapid is identified by a large concrete wall on river left as the river bends to the right. It begins with a section of class II offset ledges and culminates with a nearly river wide 3-4 ft offset ledge with a munchy hole. Certain parts of the ledge are munchier than others. The stickiest part of the hole is river right of an exposed rock in about the center of the horizon line. If you take this line, go with plenty of speed. This ledge is similar but taller post-Helene.
pointOfInterests.name: Railroad Wall a.k.a. Lost Cove

pointOfInterests.description: Maggie's Rock Rapid was buried beneath massive amounts of cobble, and is now a fairly obvious run down the right-hand channel of a steep cobble bar moving left to avoid a tree extending from the right bank.
pointOfInterests.name: Sousehole a.k.a. Maggie's Rock

pointOfInterests.description: The is the last rapid of any major consequence. Identified by an unusual orange-reddish outcropping of rock on the left by the railroad track. It has a couple offset ledges with a hole or two at the bottom depending on the water level. Super deep excellent recovery pool. Offers some form of play, from hole riding to funky fast wave surfing at nearly any water level.
pointOfInterests.name: Twin Eddies

pointOfInterests.description: This is a rock outcropping on river right that in no way resembles a dam so I couldn't tell you about the name. It has a fun little play spot at moderate water levels and apparently a really loopalicious hole develops around 5-7,000 cfs. Usually lots of sunbathers hanging out here in the summer, some clothed & some not.
pointOfInterests.name: Cherokee Dam

pointOfInterests.description: Free Parking at the U.S. Forest Service Take-out/day use area at Chestoa is on river right about 3/4 miles below the campground/USA Raft. Post Helene, this is the public take-out.
pointOfInterests.name: U.S.F.S. take out at Chestoa

alerts.title: Dangerous new rapid created by CSX
alerts.detail: CSX created a dangerous new rapid in the past few weeks. They filled in roughly the left half the riverbed with rocks at the bottom of the rapid generally where Rollercoaster used to be, forming a sloping ledge hole and pushing the flow into a nasty undercut rock. At low flows paddlers have been running left to avoid the undercut, and at medium and higher flows they have been going right of the rock. Scout on the right, but also note that the drop is at the end of a swift wave train rapid.

alerts.title: CSX Says they are Removing Rails Now
alerts.detail: CSX States: "Starting the week of February 24, 2025, and as river conditions allow, CSX workers and heavy equipment will enter the Nolichucky River to recover railroad track and ties. These materials are underwater and may be under pressure, which could create hazardous conditions for those in the area. For safety reasons, it is essential to avoid the area during these operations." The river is not closed, but be extra careful if paddling it.

alerts.title: River Wide Strainer
alerts.detail:
There is a full set or railroad tracks (both rails and ties) that leave the railroad bed on River Left and cross the entire river flow. This is below Rooster Tail. Look for tracks on River Left. Safe passage at 1000 cfs (guestimate) is on River Left where the tracks are underwater.

Hazard will vary with river level, and may shift. Please approach with caution.

alerts.title: Railraod Debris Hazards 10/25/24
alerts.detail: Rail in far right channel of second significant drop in the new Quarter Mile. It is difficult to see and just under the surface. Similar rail in left side of Doo Doo's Hole. Doo Doo's is about 0.5 miles upstream of Rock Garden, the most shallow spot on the Gorge. It used to be a water boof, now it is a tongue. Both hazards are hard to see due to the poor water quality and high turbidity.

alerts.title: Hurricane Helene
alerts.detail: WARNING: This run has been severely impacted by Hurricane Helene. Rapids are likely to have dramatically changed and access roads and parking are severely impacted or entirely gone.

(Log has been removed) There IS a log lodged between 3rd and 4th drop (Hungry Jack). Here's a captioned picture showing exactly where it is and what it looks like at 800 CFS. Watch it, you could paddle over this log and never know it is there, or roll in third drop and die wrapped around it

http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/Photo/detail/photoid/879364/size/big/

...or check most recent pic (as of this date) in photo gallery for more details.

detail.description:
The Nolichucky is in an incredibly beautiful, deep, mountain gorge that offers lots of great play, especially within the first half of the run. While the railroad on river left has a large visual presence, the Gorge remains a remote whitewater treasure. Rapids begin just around the first bend, and most of the larger rapids are within the first three miles. After a few good rapids paddlers come to Quartermile Rapid, which boasts a vertical 3-4 foot ledge that is easy to scout on river left. Rowdy rapids continue, including the super fun Roostertail rapid that features an excellent elevator ferry move. Stay heads-up for the new Rollercoaster, created by CSX in the summer of 2025, which is a Class IV drop with an undercut and a significant hole.

Its important to note that Hurricane Helene reshaped all of the Noli's rapids in September of 2024 except perhaps Entrance Rapid. The rapids in the Gorge are not just different - they are completely different and utterly unrecognizeable. Paddlers can expect a more channelzed river than before the storm, with more punch, much better play, and lower good flow ranges. It is perhaps slightly harder than before the storm, and most paddlers feel the rapids are better and the paddle-out goes much more quickly.

**Parking at the takeout:** Free parking is available at the US Forest Service Chestoa day use area.

**Poplar Put In:** The Forest Service is once again allowing public access following a 16 month closure.

**Shuttle Information /** **Shuttles** The one-way shuttle takes about 30 minutes meaning an hour at the end of your day if you don't use a shuttle service. Given the time, gas, and wear & tear on your vehicle, most boaters choose to use a shuttle service rather than make a 2nd trip at the end of the day. You pick up a pre-arranged shuttle driver at the takeout, then you drive to the put-in with the driver. While you are on the river, the driver drops your vehicle off at the takeout. There are other options, described below where you don't use your own vehicle. For all the shuttle services, give them some advance notice--like when you leave you house in the am and on busy weekends the day before. **Uncle Johnny's Hostel**- has shuttle drivers for the same $25. You can park at the Hostel or at Chestoa (preferred). Phone - 423-735-0548. E-mail [Unclejohnnys2000@yahoo.com ](mailto:Unclejohnnys2000@yahoo.com)**Private Shuttle Drivers -** So far I have Jan & Matt Buzan, who live at the takeout. They have day jobs and are not always available but usually one of them is available.phone 386-801-0331. Hoping to expand the list of private shuttle drivers over time.
